result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
An error boundary event is always interrupting (cancelActivity=true); a cancel boundary event is used only on a transaction subProcess.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Attach a boundary event with attachedToRef. Set cancelActivity=true when it interrupts the activity and false only for supported non-interrupting behavior.
Attach to an activity boundary only these triggers: message, timer, escalation, conditional, signal, error, cancel, compensation or multiple. Never a none or link event.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

result.rule: When the description says an external device or party keeps sending back status or updates while the actor performs other work at the same time: Model the receipt of these ongoing updates as its own intermediate catch event on a branch that runs in parallel with the actor's other work, and do not omit it. Do not model it as a receive task, because the wait is for a recurring message rather than a unit of work. Join the branch back to the main flow when the work it supports completes.

When The description says the process sends a request or order to an outside party and then continues only after a reply, confirmation, or status arrives, so the next decision or step depends on that reply.: Model the wait for that reply as its own step placed directly after the sending step and before the next decision or activity. Use a receive activity (bpmn:receiveTask) when receiving the reply is the unit of work, or an intermediate catch event when the wait is only a pause. Connect the send step, the receive step, and the next element with sequence flows, and do not let the flow skip from the send step straight to the decision.

When the description states that an actor may postpone a stated activity while other pending work is handled, so the activity happens only on a condition: Model the postponable activity itself as a task labeled with the activity named in the description. Place it on the branch that the stated condition selects, behind an exclusive decision gateway whose outcomes separate the postponed case from the immediate case. Do not reduce the deferral to a gateway branch that leads only to the other pending work.

When the description says an actor sends requests to several external parties asking for proposals, and then, in a separate step, says that the actor selects one of those parties, so the selection depends on the proposals received: Model the selection as its own bpmn:task, labeled with the selection action the description names, placed on the sequence flow after the task that sends the requests and before any gateway or activity that depends on the selection. Do not merge the selection into the request task and do not omit it, even when the description states the selection in a separate sentence or treats it as a consequence of the requests.
